papers.title: An amygdala-mediated simulation-to-decision cascade aligns interbrain dynamics to solve social dilemmas.
papers.abstract: Mutual cooperation (MC) requires independent decision-makers to coordinate under uncertainty about each other's intentions. Using simultaneous intracranial electroencephalography from epilepsy-patient dyads playing a real-time iterated prisoner's dilemma, we identified neurocognitive mechanisms that enable interacting brains to align during mutual cooperation. Amygdala interbrain representational alignment (IBRA), similarity in fine-grained neural spectral patterns across partners, emerged selectively during MC and predicted trial-by-trial outcomes. Early θ-suppression-characterized IBRA reflected rapid, history-sensitive alignment, whereas later IBRA, characterized by low-frequency suppression and γ increases, supported coordinated commitment and action. Furthermore, mutual cooperation relied on an amygdala-mediated, simulation-to-decision cascade, operationalized here as a model-based prospective estimate of partner cooperation that guided self-choice. Amygdala low-frequency suppression tracked this prospective estimate of partner cooperation and θ-γ coupling linked this partner estimate to self-decision processes. Conditional cooperators strategically relied on partner tracking, whereas unconditional cooperators leveraged dispositional tolerance of uncertainty to transition into anticipatory neural alignment. These findings reveal the neural interdependency underpinning MC, redefining cooperation not as isolated decision-making but as a dynamic, interbrain, cognitive alignment.

papers.title: Disentangling microbiota-dependent and -independent impacts of antibiotics on host physiology.
papers.abstract: Antibiotics are believed to affect host physiology by altering the gut microbiota. However, it remains unclear which effects of antibiotics are microbiota dependent and which are microbiota independent. Here we present a resource encompassing host and microbiota responses to antibiotic treatment and a computational tool with which to analyse them. Metagenomic and transcriptomic analyses of conventional and germ-free mice revealed that antibiotic administration routes and their combinations affect host and microbiota responses. We developed CompoRes-a computational tool that distinguishes the microbiota-independent impact of antibiotic-induced perturbations, revealing that antibiotics directly impact host physiology. We found that diurnal expression of major histocompatibility complex class II in the mouse colon is controlled by glucose via feeding. This pattern was lost during antibiotic treatment as vancomycin altered feeding behaviour in a microbiota-independent and evolutionarily conserved manner. Together, our study establishes a direct, non-microbial pathway by which antibiotics reshape host immunity and circadian physiology.

papers.title: Considering counterfactual prediction models in sleep research: A demonstration of incident stroke prediction in an observational cohort study.
papers.abstract: Data-driven risk prediction algorithms are increasingly common. However, studies suggesting that a single set of variables are most "important" within a given risk prediction model ignore the reality that other equally useful models containing entirely different features may exist. We aim to use a novel approach (Model Path Selection) to demonstrate that, for any given health outcome, there are likely many comparable counterfactual models including different sets of variables. We focus on incident stroke as a scientifically meaningful outcome to motivate this demonstration. Model Path Selection uses an iterative model-building procedure to illustrate a set of counterfactual prediction models ("paths"). We applied Model Path Selection to Sleep Heart Health Study data (N = 4,512 adults) to predict 5-year incident stroke, considering 30 features comprising demographics, self-reported and measured medical risk factors, polysomnography, and self-reported sleep. Area Under the Curve was estimated for each resulting path based on 10-fold cross-validation. Model Path Selection identified 61 unique counterfactual models. 13 of these achieved Area Under the Curves between 0.81 and 0.82. Area Under the Curves of the remaining models ranged from 0.53 to 0.68 (median 0.61). All 13 top models included age plus various combinations of other features (polysomnography indices, body mass index, and/or the Short Form 36 mental and physical component scores). Model Path Selection can illuminate counterfactual prediction models, differentiate features that may be uniquely predictive from those that can be swapped out with other features, enhance reproducibility, inform the design of clinically practical predictive tools, and suggest sleep-related risk factors to be targeted for health promotion.

papers.title: Sociodemographic correlates of daytime napping in Canadian preschoolers.
papers.abstract: To examine the sociodemographic and sleep-related characteristics of Canadian children aged 3 to 4 years who napped compared with those who did not. This cross-sectional study used data from the 2023 Canadian Health Survey on Children and Youth (CHSCY), a nationally representative survey. Parents of children aged 3 to 4 years (n=6291) reported napping status, nap duration, nighttime sleep characteristics, and sociodemographic factors. Weighted proportions and chi-square tests compared nappers and non-nappers. Multivariable logistic regression identified sociodemographic characteristics independently associated with daytime napping. Napping prevalence was lower among 4-year-olds than 3-year-olds (27.6% vs. 48.7%, P<.001). Children who napped were more likely to be from non-White ethnoracial backgrounds, live in lower-income households, and have landed immigrant status, whereas non-nappers were more often White, from higher-income households, and Canadian-born. After multivariable adjustment, Black and Arab/West Asian children had higher odds of daytime napping, whereas Indigenous children had lower odds than White children. Immigration status was no longer independently associated with daytime napping. No significant differences were observed by gender, parental education, or perceived general or mental health. Non-nappers were more likely to obtain at least 10 hours of nighttime sleep (3 years: 95.4% vs. 79.4%, P<.001; 4 years: 90.1% vs. 76.7%, P<.001) and, at age 3, to fall asleep within 10 minutes at night (55.3% vs. 39.7%, P<.001). Among 4-year-olds, nappers were more likely to report no or almost never experiencing nighttime awakenings (57.3% vs. 44.3%, P<.001). Mean nap duration remained stable at approximately 2.4 to 2.5 hours. Daytime napping in Canadian preschoolers varies by developmental stage and sociodemographic characteristics, supporting previous evidence that sleep patterns during the preschool years reflect both developmental variability and contextual influences.

papers.title: Amplitude-integrated electroencephalogram (aEEG): A bedside window into newborn brain function in the NICU.
papers.abstract: Amplitude-integrated electroencephalography (aEEG) remains an important tool for bedside neonatal brain monitoring. The rapid application of aEEG offers critical practical advantages for bedside clinicians assessing infants at risk for brain injury. aEEG has a distinct clinical niche in evaluations for hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) and as a first-line tool for seizure detection, alongside conventional video electroencephalogram (cEEG). Ultimately, the integration of aEEG with a broader multimodal neuromonitoring framework enhances neurodevelopmental prognostication and facilitates individualized bedside interventions, solidifying its relevance in contemporary neonatal neurocritical care.

papers.title: Lung Restriction From Childhood Is Associated With Obstructive Sleep Apnoea in Middle-Age.
papers.abstract: Whether lifetime lung function trajectories and spirometry patterns are associated with Obstructive Sleep Apnoea (OSA) is unknown. We aimed to investigate this association to widen the understanding of OSA pathophysiology. We previously identified six FEV1/FVC (forced expiratory volume in the first second/forced vital capacity) and five FVC trajectories within a population-based prospective cohort (n = 2422) using spirometry assessed at ages 7, 13, 18, 43, 50, and 53 years. These trajectories were combined into four lifetime spirometry patterns: restrictive-only, obstructive-only, mixed, and reference (normal), which were our exposure variables. Outcomes were medically-confirmed OSA in midlife and probable-OSA defined using the STOP-Bang questionnaire. Associations were assessed using logistic regression models. The 'restrictive-only' spirometry pattern was associated with medically-confirmed OSA (OR = 2.5; 95% CI 1.5, 4.3). In addition, restriction-confirmatory low total lung capacity and reduced functional residual capacity were associated with increased odds of medically-confirmed OSA (OR = 1.4; 0.9, 2.1 and OR = 1.7; 1.1, 2.6, respectively, per one SD reduction in volume). The results were similar for probable OSA. These associations held when controlled for BMI and central obesity and were independent of childhood lung function. Neither transfer factor for carbon monoxide (TLco) nor transfer coefficient (Kco) was associated with OSA. We provide first evidence that lifetime lung restriction is related to middle-age OSA. While this information may be used to incidentally flag middle-age OSA risk and vice versa, further research is encouraged to confirm the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms.

papers.title: Wide dynamic range of contrast-encoding in neural responses in macaque V1.
papers.abstract: The dynamic range of contrast-encoding in the early visual system has been investigated at both single-neuron and population levels in animals using oriented stimuli such as gratings and Gabor patches. However, contrast-encoding of unoriented stimuli such as Gaussians has been less explored, even though such stimuli can evoke a large population response. In studies that employ Gaussians, contrast response functions (CRFs) of neurons and neural populations in primary visual cortex are typically characterized across a limited range of Weber contrasts up to 100%, which may not adequately reflect the statistics of contrast in natural scenes. Indeed, our preliminary analysis shows that locations with center-surround contrasts far exceeding the level comparable to a Gaussian stimulus of 100% Weber contrast are ubiquitous in natural scenes. Thus, our current understanding of contrast encoding remains incomplete in the context of natural environments. Here, we measured spiking activities of individual neurons using electrophysiology and population responses using widefield calcium imaging in V1 of fixating male macaques (Macaca mulatta) while Gaussian stimuli were presented over a wide range of Weber contrasts, up to 900%. Both the average spiking response and the average population response continued to increase robustly above 100% Weber contrast. Only a small minority of neurons saturated below 100% Weber contrast. These results demonstrate that the dynamic range of contrast-encoding in V1 is broader than previously assumed and aligns more closely with the statistics of contrast in natural scenes.Significance Statement The dynamic range of contrast-encoding in V1 has typically been characterized using only a limited range of contrasts, often excluding the high contrasts commonly found in natural scenes. We measured contrast response functions of individual neurons and neural populations in V1 across a much wider range of contrasts. We found that the responses of the majority of neurons, as well as the overall population, increased robustly up to extremely high contrasts. These findings suggest that the dynamic range of contrast encoding in V1 extends well beyond the commonly tested range.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience

papers.title: Late Integration of Prior Expectations During Precision-Weighted Perceptual Decisions.
papers.abstract: Adaptive perceptual decision-making relies on the ability to combine sensory evidence with prior expectations in a precision-weighted manner. Although Bayesian inference provides a clear normative account of how such integration should occur, the neural mechanisms through which the brain represents and combines priors and likelihoods remain poorly understood. Across two preregistered experiments, we investigated how the precision of learned priors and sensory likelihoods influence visual motion judgements and associated neural activity patterns during a random-dot motion estimation task. Neurotypical adult participants (N=80, 58 female) reported directions of visual motion stimuli, with motion coherence varying randomly across trials. Prior expectations over the continuous motion direction space were manipulated block-wise by implicitly varying the probabilities with which different motion directions were presented. Consistent with precision-weighted inference, response accuracy improved as motion coherence increased with robust response biases toward the expected motion direction. Neural activity measured using electroencephalography (EEG) revealed reliable effects of prior expectation on the univariate central-parietal positivity (CPP), consistent with reduced accumulation of sensory evidence under informative priors. Multivariate analysis using inverted-encoding models revealed robust effects of prior precision on stimulus-specific neural representations, but only late, during response planning stages. Together, these findings suggest that priors learned over a continuous space do not modulate the encoding of sensory evidence and are instead integrated later in the decision-process.Significance Statement Perceptual decisions require combining noisy sensory input with prior expectations about what is likely to occur. It remains unclear how the brain integrates prior expectations with incoming sensory evidence. Using a visual motion task and concurrent brain imaging, we show that expectations do not alter early stimulus-encoding, but are instead integrated at later stages of decision formation and action planning. These findings add nuance to influential theories proposing that learned expectations directly affect stimulus representations and instead highlight their contribution to later decision-related processes. This work advances understanding of how the brain uses experience to optimise perceptual decisions under uncertainty.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience

papers.title: MRI Characterization of Structural Brain Abnormalities in NGLY1 Deficiency.
papers.abstract: NGLY1 (N-Glycanase 1) deficiency is an ultrarare autosomal recessive disorder affecting ~165 patients worldwide, characterized by developmental delay, hyperkinetic movement disorders and shortened life expectancy. Despite its severe neurological manifestations, comprehensive neuroimaging characterization has been limited to case reports and small descriptive studies. Our objective was to investigate alterations in brain morphology in patients with NGLY1 deficiency and determine whether these metrics associate with clinical phenotypes. This case series analysed real-world MRI scans performed on 11 patients with molecularly diagnosed NGLY1 deficiency between 1999 and 2023 at sites across the globe. Ages ranged from 2 to 19 years at scan time (five female and six male). Cortical and subcortical morphology, including subcortical volume and cortical thickness, surface area, volume and curvature, was measured with three-dimensional T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans. Z scores were calculated using normative models from CentileBrain for patients > 3 years old or custom models for patients < 3 years old. Clinical phenotypes were matched to Human Phenotype Ontology codes. Sixteen scans from 11 patients met quality criteria for analysis. Both age groups (under and over 3 years old) showed significantly reduced subcortical volumes, particularly in bilateral thalamus and putamen. Younger patients demonstrated widespread reductions in cortical surface area, volume and curvature, indicating altered gyrification patterns. Older patients showed thinner dorsal and thicker ventral cortical regions with limited surface area reductions. Thalamic volume reduction in older patients correlated with gait disturbance, dysphagia and EEG abnormalities, with additional cortical associations with sleep and hearing abnormalities. Seizure presence in younger patients correlated with altered cortical thickness, surface area and curvature patterns. NGLY1 deficiency is associated with pervasive alterations in brain development affecting both subcortical and cortical morphology. Age-dependent patterns of cortical alterations indicate disrupted neurodevelopmental trajectories that may reflect impaired neuronal migration and/or altered synaptic pruning. Correlations with clinical variables suggest that these measures may serve as useful biomarkers for tracking disease progression and/or treatment efficacy. These findings provide a comprehensive neuroimaging characterization of NGLY1 Deficiency and establish a foundation for understanding brain structure-function relationships in this ultrarare disorder.
papers.journal: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience

papers.title: Cross-Modal Masked Connectome Transformer for multimodal EEG-fMRI learning in ADHD diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is associated with distributed alterations in large-scale brain systems, making reliable diagnosis from neuroimaging data challenging. EEG-derived and fMRI-derived static functional-connectivity profiles summarize patterns of electrophysiological coupling and hemodynamic covariation, respectively, but their heterogeneous signal mechanisms make direct multimodal alignment difficult. We propose a Cross-Modal Masked Connectome Transformer (CM-MCT) for EEG-fMRI based ADHD diagnosis. Instead of imposing direct correspondence between individual connections, CM-MCT treats each Desikan-Killiany 68-region cortical atlas (DK-68) region of interest (ROI) as a connectivity-profile token and learns to recover masked ROI-level connectome information within and across modalities. The model contains modality-specific Transformer encoders, cross-modal masked connectome objectives, and a bidirectional cross-attention fusion module for diagnostic prediction. Cross-fitted mask perturbations are used to characterize ROI-level model dependence, with explicit assessment of associations with nodal strength and perturbation magnitude. Experiments using repeated five-by-five stratified evaluation of 210 paired HBN subjects demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 89.7% accuracy (95% confidence interval: 85.7%-93.3%) and 94.3% AUC (95% confidence interval: 91.5%-96.8%). Compared with the evaluated methods under matched splits, preprocessing, validation, and model-selection rules, CM-MCT shows the highest mean performance, although the AUC difference from the strongest baseline does not reach statistical significance after multiplicity correction. CM-MCT supports multimodal learning from the complementary network-level information provided by static EEG and fMRI connectivity profiles. Perturbation analysis yields modality-specific ROI sensitivity patterns that are modestly associated with the assessed factors. These heatmaps characterize model dependence without establishing causal involvement or identifying ADHD biomarkers.

papers.title: Effects of Aromatherapy on The pain-anxiety-Sleep disturbance Symptom Cluster in Breast Cancer Patients A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of aromatherapy on the pain-anxiety-sleep disturbance symptom cluster in breast cancer patients. Randomized Controlled Trials were searched in CNKI, Wanfang, PubMed, Scopus, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library before August 2026. The screening of literature and data extraction were independently completed by two researchers, and the ROB 2 was used to evaluate the risk of bias. A narrative method was used to synthesize the outcomes. This systematic review has been registered(PROSPERO: CRD420251132362). 10 articles were included. 7 studies assessed at least two symptoms within the pain-anxiety-sleep disturbance symptom cluster. Effective part of the intervention including the interventions length within 4 weeks, the optimal timing for intervention were in the evening, The intervention time should be limited within 20-30min. Aromatherapy may be a potential adjunctive therapy for alleviating the pain-anxiety-sleep disturbance symptom cluster in breast cancer patients across different treatment phases. But higher-quality studies with rigorous designs and standardized reporting are needed before clinical implementation can be recommended.

papers.title: Neural Response to Monetary and Social Feedback in Childhood: Processing Reward and Loss in Relation to Peer Outcomes and Anxiety Symptoms.
papers.abstract: Anxiety disorders are the most prevalent psychiatric conditions in childhood and are associated with social functioning impairment. How youth process rewards may contribute to the development of social impairment in childhood anxiety. Although aberrant reward processing is a well-established mechanism of psychopathology, associations with anxiety remain inconsistent and limited, especially in childhood. This study investigated neural response to monetary and social reward feedback in relation to anxiety and peer functioning in children. Children (N=106; Age=8.12±.68 years) completed the Doors Task and the Island Getaway Task while electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings assessed event-related potentials (ERPs) to wins and losses. Parents completed questionnaires assessing child anxiety, depression, and peer relations. Contrary to pre-registered hypotheses, we found a significant Valence (reward versus loss) by Condition (monetary versus social) interaction. Specifically, children exhibited greater neural response to monetary loss than reward, but showed the opposite pattern in the social condition, with greater neural response to social reward than loss. Higher child- and parent-reported total and generalized anxiety predicted significantly greater neural response to monetary reward, but not monetary loss or social feedback. As hypothesized, anxiety symptoms significantly moderated the association between neural response and peer relations, demonstrating that for highly anxious children, a greater neural response to social loss predicted worse peer relations. Findings demonstrate differences in neural response to monetary and social feedback processing. Moreover, the distinct vulnerability to social rejection might impair peer functioning in anxious children, suggesting that clinical interventions targeting social rejection processing may effectively improve peer outcomes in childhood anxiety.

papers.title: Circadian and Sleep-Wake Modulation of EEG Functional Connectivity Across Brain States and Its Associations With Cognition in Humans.
papers.abstract: Sleep and circadian rhythms both influence human brain function, but their distinct contributions to large-scale network organization remain unclear. We quantified the effect of brain state (wake, NREM, REM), sleep-wake history, and circadian phase on functional connectivity using over 1,200 hours of artifact-free EEG recorded during a 10-day forced-desynchrony protocol. We derived principal components of functional connectivity and found that both sleep-wake history and circadian phase significantly modulated functional connectivity, with sleep-wake history exerting a broader influence. Complementary cosinor analyses further demonstrated circadian rhythmicity in several NREM and REM connectivity measures. Across sleep, global connectivity increased progressively during NREM sleep, particularly in the delta and sigma bands, but declined during REM sleep. During controlled resting wakefulness, increasing time awake was associated with higher global alpha-band connectivity, which was associated with poorer concurrent cognitive performance. Connectivity during NREM sleep was also associated with subsequent cognitive performance, with lower global theta and, to a lesser extent, higher sigma connectivity linked to better performance. REM connectivity was not associated with these cognitive measures. Together, these findings reveal opposing NREM and REM trajectories in large-scale EEG functional connectivity and show that these brain-state-specific network dynamics are shaped by both sleep-wake history and circadian phase and are associated with cognitive performance.

papers.title: EEG Resting-State Beta Band Dynamic Functional Connectivity Reveals State-Dependent Disruption of Language Network Lateralisation in First-Episode Schizophrenia.
papers.abstract: Language disorganisation is a core feature of schizophrenia with significant functional consequences. However, its neurophysiological substrates remain poorly characterised, particularly in the early stages of the illness. This study investigated whether first-episode schizophrenia (FES) is associated with disruption in the organisation of language-network lateralisation, using both static and dynamic functional connectivity metrics in the EEG beta band. Thirty-one FES patients and 32 age-matched healthy volunteer subjects (HVS) underwent resting-state 64-channel EEG. Source-level connectivity was estimated using the weighted phase lag index with sliding windows, yielding 979 connectivity matrices per participant. Brain network states (BNS) were identified via k-means clustering. Static connectivity was obtained by time-averaging. Temporal features, graph-theoretical metrics, and language-network laterality indices were extracted for both whole-network and language-specific analyses. Group comparisons used permutation-based tests with family-wise error correction. Static connectivity yielded no significant group differences in any metric. Dynamic analysis identified six BNS. FES showed a significant increase in the variability of the temporal dynamics and graph-theory features of BNS5, a state characterised by parieto-occipital dominance. The core language network laterality index was significantly reduced in FES within BNS1, a state characterised by auditory-visual dominance. BNS1 occurrence correlated negatively with language disorganisation scores. Dynamic BNS-specific language network metrics correlated with verbal fluency performance exclusively in FES. These findings demonstrate that language dysfunction in early psychosis is expressed as state-dependent disruption of brain network stability and language lateralisation, detectable only through dynamic connectivity analysis.

papers.title: Effects of LBBAP Pacing-Site Position under a Modelled Proximal LBBB: A 24-Model Electrophysiological Simulation Study.
papers.abstract: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) may recruit the distal left-sided conduction system, but the electrical effect of pacing-site position along the left bundle branch (LBB) remains incompletely defined. We evaluated this effect in 24 four-chamber virtual heart anatomies using a Reaction-Eikonal finite-element model with rule-based myocardial fibres and algorithmically generated His-Purkinje networks. A modelled proximal Histo-LBB disconnection preserved the distal LBB-Purkinje network while interrupting its proximal connection. Six conditions were simulated in each anatomy: a sinoatrial-node (SAN)-initiated left bundle branch block (LBBB) control, right ventricular apical pacing, right ventricular outflow-tract pacing and a modelled non-selective LBB capture configuration at proximal, nominal and distal positions. The primary outcome was BiV_TAT95, the 95th percentile of activation times across left-ventricular, rightventricular and interventricular-septal nodes. The control-versus-paced analysis used a common simulation-clock origin and was interpreted as contextual benchmarking, whereas the positional analysis used matched direct ventricular stimulation. In the matched positional analysis, median BiV_TAT95 was 104.5, 93.5 and 88.5 ms for proximal, nominal and distal LBBAP, respectively (Friedman chi-square = 48.000, P < 0.001, Kendall's W = 1.000); every anatomy followed distal < nominal < proximal. In three selected anatomies, a 20% decrease or increase in the prescribed myocardial conduction speeds altered absolute activation times but preserved this ordering in all nine anatomy-by-speed combinations. Under the tested homogeneous substrate and modelled non-selective capture configuration, the distal tested position produced the lowest simulated BiV_TAT95; this does not imply superiority for every activation metric. This conditional prediction requires validation against patient-specific electrical data.

papers.title: An acetylcholine-inhibited sleep-active hippocampal interneuron orchestrates memory consolidation.
papers.abstract: Memory reactivation during hippocampal ripples is critical for sleep-dependent memory consolidation. However, the molecular-to-circuit mechanism enabling sleep-predominant ripple generation remains unresolved. Here, we discovered that a sparse population of GABAergic interneurons in the mouse hippocampus specializes in gating ripple generation and memory consolidation. While all known genetically labeled hippocampal interneurons were highly active during wakefulness and rapid-eye-movement (REM) sleep, genetic targeting of M2 acetylcholine receptor (Chrm2)-expressing neurons isolated a specific population preferentially active during non-REM (NREM) sleep and quiet wakefulness. These acetylcholine-inhibited interneurons inhibited the entire hippocampus in an infra-slow rhythm (∼0.015 Hz). Suppressing their activity in dorsal CA3 or ventral hippocampus impaired spatial and social memory, respectively. Furthermore, Chrm2+ neurons were closely associated with ripples; their activity bidirectionally modulated ripple occurrence via widespread inhibition. Thus, Chrm2+ interneurons are critical in linking neuromodulatory state to memory consolidation, offering genetically targeted access to sleep-active memory circuits implicated in cognitive disorders.

papers.title: Stage-specific contributions of dorsal and ventral premotor cortices to the acquisition of arbitrary visuomotor associations.
papers.abstract: The acquisition and consolidation of arbitrary visuomotor mappings (AVMMs) engage premotor regions, yet the distinct contributions of the dorsal (PMd) and ventral (PMv) premotor cortices remain unclear. Here, we applied continuous theta-burst stimulation (cTBS) immediately before AVMM learning to transiently disrupt PMd, PMv, or an occipital control site (V1) in 19 healthy young adults, using a within-subjects design. Participants learned arbitrary stimulus-response associations through trial-and-error feedback and completed a 24-h delayed recall test. Trial-by-trial accuracy and response times were modeled using state-space and Rescorla-Wagner frameworks to quantify learning dynamics, prediction errors, and stabilization across days. Disruption of both PMd and PMv slowed early acquisition of AVMMs to a comparable extent relative to V1. However, only PMd disruption additionally impaired next-day recall, rendering recall performance dependent on sleep quality and decoupled from learning-day performance, whereas recall following PMv disruption remained comparable to the control condition. These findings indicate that PMd, but not PMv, contributes to the stabilization of newly learned visuomotor associations, providing causal, stage-specific evidence for a functional dissociation within the human premotor cortex: PMd and PMv support early rule formation and exploratory learning, whereas only PMd contributes to subsequent stabilization of newly learned visuomotor associations. Furthermore, they emphasize the modulatory influence of sleep on memory retention when consolidation processes are compromised, advancing mechanistic models of premotor contributions to associative sensorimotor learning.

papers.title: Psychological violence, subjective well-being, and burnout among healthcare workers: The roles of sleep disturbance and perceived occupational infection risk.
papers.abstract: Psychological violence (PCV), which includes verbal abuse, bullying, intimidation, sexual harassment and ethnic discrimination, is the most frequently reported form of workplace violence in health care and a well-documented correlate of burnout. Healthcare workers (HCWs) in infectious disease services face this psychosocial hazard alongside two further, structurally persistent conditions: impaired recovery through disturbed sleep, and the appraised risk of acquiring infection at work. How these demands combine with workers' personal psychological resources is not well understood. To examine (i) whether PCV exposure is associated with burnout, (ii) whether subjective well-being (SWB) functions as an intervening variable in that association, (iii) whether sleep disturbance is associated with burnout independently of SWB, and (iv) whether the strength of the SWB-burnout association depends on the level of perceived occupational infection risk. Cross-sectional survey of 675 HCWs (76.3% women) at a public tertiary infectious disease hospital in southern China (December 2022 - January 2023), a designated centre for HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, hepatitis and, at the time of data collection, COVID-19. PCV exposure over the preceding 12 months was assessed with the ILO/ICN/WHO/PSI instrument; SWB with the WHO-5; burnout with the two-item abbreviated Maslach Burnout Inventory screen; sleep disturbance with three binary epidemiological items; and perceived occupational infection risk with a single validated item indexing appraised infection hazard in the respondent's own workplace. Conditional process analysis (ordinary least squares path analysis, 5000 bootstrap resamples) was adjusted for gender, age band, education, occupation, employment type, department and reported concern about workplace violence. PCV was reported by 34.1% of participants and sleep disturbance by 53.3%. PCV exposure was positively associated with burnout (adjusted direct association b = 0.53, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.96, P = .015; total association b = 0.72, 95% CI 0.27 to 1.19). SWB was negatively associated with burnout (b = -0.13, P < .001) and accounted for an indirect association of 0.19 (95% CI 0.05 to 0.34), approximately 26% of the total. Sleep disturbance was independently associated with burnout after adjustment for SWB and all covariates (b = 0.46 per additional sleep symptom, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.68, P < .001). Perceived occupational infection risk moderated the SWB-burnout association (interaction b = -0.038, 95% CI -0.060 to -0.016, P < .001): the association between SWB and burnout was steeper at higher perceived risk (b = -0.085 at -1 SD; -0.133 at the mean; -0.181 at +1 SD), and the conditional indirect association rose correspondingly (0.12 to 0.26; index of moderated mediation 0.054, 95% CI 0.012 to 0.112). In a workforce facing sustained occupational infection risk, PCV exposure, low SWB and disturbed sleep were each associated with greater burnout, and SWB differentiated burnout most sharply among workers appraising their workplace as most hazardous. Because the design is cross-sectional, the direction of the PCV-SWB-burnout sequence cannot be established, and reciprocal influence is likely. The findings support treating violence prevention, recovery-protective scheduling and infection-risk communication as complementary components of occupational mental health provision rather than as separate programmes.

papers.title: Cognitively demanding motor exercise and subsequent inhibitory control: Behavioral and ERP Evidence.
papers.abstract: Acute exercise can influence executive function, yet conventional exercise prescriptions primarily characterize its physical dose and rarely specify the cognitive operations embedded within the exercise bout. Using a Motor-Cognitive Integrated Task (MCIT) with conditions differing in cognitive demand while involving comparable physical demands, this study examined whether cognitively demanding motor exercise was associated with differences in subsequent behavioral and neurophysiological indices of inhibitory control. Forty healthy young adults completed two counterbalanced sessions separated by at least 24 h. In the experimental session, participants performed the MCIT, which required whole-body responses to flanker stimuli. In the control session, participants performed the same motor task in response to predictable single-arrow stimuli. Heart rate (HR), physical rating of perceived exertion (RPE), cognitive RPE, response time (RT), movement time (MT), and overall response time (RMT) were assessed during the MCIT. Immediately afterward, participants completed a computerized flanker task while electroencephalography was recorded. Cognitive RPE, RT and RMT of the MCIT were higher in the experimental session than in the control session, whereas HR, physical RPE, and MT of the MCIT were comparable across sessions. Following the MCIT, participants showed a smaller flanker interference in the experimental than in the control session, accompanied by differences in conflict-related modulation of the N2 and smaller overall P3 amplitude, with no between-session difference in accuracy. Cognitive demand may represent a manipulable characteristic of acute exercise prescription beyond physical intensity alone. Motor exercise incorporating greater cognitive demands was associated with reduced subsequent behavioral interference and differences in N2 and P3 modulation. Although these effects cannot be attributed exclusively to any specific cognitive operation, the findings highlight the potential importance of considering the cognitive characteristics of exercise when examining its acute neurocognitive effects.

papers.title: A spatio-temporal attention convolutional network with topology-preserving channel embedding and transformer for EEG decoding.
papers.abstract: EEG-based BCI has shown promising applications in motor rehabilitation and emotion recognition. Given the non-stationarity and variability of EEG signals, it is essential to develop classification models that can effectively extract spatio-temporal features while maintaining strong generalization capabilities. This paper proposes a spatio-temporal attention convolutional network for EEG decoding (E-STACNet) to encode the topological features and temporal characteristics of EEG signals within a unified network framework. It consists of channel-attention (CA) block, convolutional (CV) layers, multi-head self-attention (MSA) and classifier layer. Specifically, CA block encodes spatial topological feature via a topology-preserving channel embedding method. Then convolutional layers are employed to encode low-level temporal information and further extract spatial features, followed by MSA block to highlight the most important temporal information of EEG signals. Finally, the outputs are obtained through two fully-connected layers. We conducted experiments on three public EEG-based datasets including BCI Competition IV dataset 2a, Giga DB and DEAP. The results demonstrate E-STACNet achieves average accuracies of 88.00% and 80.62% on datasets 2a and Giga DB, respectively. On the DEAP, it reaches average accuracies of 96.49% and 96.46% for valence and arousal. The proposed model outperforms other state-of-the-art models on all three datasets. Additionally, the ablation study reveals the importance of topology-preserving channel embedding for the proposed network. Visualization analysis shows E-STACNet could obtain the importance of channels at different locations through the channel-attention mechanism, which demonstrates the interpretability of the proposed model. Overall, the accurate and generalization capabilities of E-STACNet will promote the development of EEG-based BCIs.

papers.title: Sleep duration and risk of microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes: A prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Longitudinal evidence on sleep duration's effects on type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) microvascular outcomes, particularly in Asian populations, remains limited. This study investigated the prospective association between sleep duration and microvascular complication incidence in T2DM patients. This prospective cohort included 1236 T2DM adults, free of microvascular complications at baseline from National Metabolic Management Centre Ningbo Branch (2018-2023). Self-reported sleep duration was categorized into 5 groups (<7, 7-8, 8-9, 9-10, or ≥10h). Incident diabetic kidney disease (DKD), retinopathy (DR), and peripheral neuropathy (DPN) were ascertained. Cox regression and restricted cubic spline analyses estimated hazard ratio (HRs) and dose-response relationships. In 2459 person-years, 237 participants developed microvascular complications. A U-shaped association emerged between sleep duration and composite microvascular complications (P < 0.001) and DPN (P = 0.039), with lowest risk at 7-8h. Compared to 7-8h, shorter (<7h) and longer (≥10h) durations significantly increased composite microvascular complication risks (HR = 1.71, P = 0.018; HR = 1.87, P = 0.005). No statistically significant interactions were observed between sleep duration and age, BMI, sedentary time, or sleep quality (all P for interaction >0.05). Both insufficient and excessive sleep increase T2DM microvascular complication risks. Maintaining 7-8 h of sleep daily may be a vital behavioral target in comprehensive T2DM management, potentially reducing microvascular complication burden.

papers.title: Three-month follow-up after discontinuation of steam-assisted respiratory muscle training in mild-to-moderate obstructive sleep apnea: an exploratory polysomnographic study.
papers.abstract: To explore polysomnographic findings three months after discontinuation of steam-assisted respiratory muscle training (RMT) in mild-to-moderate obstructive sleep apnea. This exploratory secondary follow-up included 33 of 48 intervention entrants who completed polysomnography at baseline, after 12 weeks of training, and three months after cessation. The primary analysis used repeated-measures ANOVA (RM-ANOVA). Distributional diagnostics and exact Friedman sensitivity analyses were conducted for eight sleep-stage and periodic limb movement outcomes. Conventional respiratory-event indices showed no overall time effect (all p ≥ 0.3). Flow limitation differed across visits (p = 0.02), without an immediate post-intervention reduction. The RM-ANOVA identified visit differences in REM latency (169.9 ± 74.9 min at baseline, 138.8 ± 66.4 min post-intervention, and 134.0 ± 66.5 min at follow-up; p = 0.003), N1 proportion (6.6 ± 4.0%, 10.8 ± 5.9%, and 11.2 ± 6.1%, respectively; p = 0.002), and PLMS-related arousal index (1.3 ± 2.1/h, 0.6 ± 1.1/h, and 0.7 ± 1.4/h, respectively; p = 0.01) and count (9.3 ± 15.2, 4.3 ± 7.9, and 5.2 ± 10.0, respectively; p = 0.02). Exact Friedman analyses yielded visit differences for N1 (p = 0.002) and the PLMS-related arousal index and count (p = 0.01 and 0.02), but not REM latency (p = 0.1). This exploratory follow-up identified differences in N1 proportion and PLMS-related arousal measures across visits, supported by sensitivity analyses, while no overall visit differences were detected in conventional respiratory-event indices. REM latency differed significantly across visits in RM-ANOVA, but not in the sensitivity analysis. These observations warrant further investigation in controlled studies; the single-arm design and absence of an adaptation night prevent attribution to steam-assisted RMT or confirmation of lasting clinical benefit. papers.title: A systematic review of machine learning approaches for sleep posture recognition across sensing modalities (2023-2025).
papers.abstract: Sleep posture directly affects sleep quality, respiratory function, and musculoskeletal health. Machine learning (ML) techniques have been increasingly applied to automatic sleep posture recognition across diverse sensing modalities. However, direct comparisons across existing studies remain difficult due to widespread reliance on small, private datasets and inconsistent evaluation protocols, which limit the generalizability of reported findings. This review aims to systematically characterize recent ML-based research on sleep posture recognition, identify methodological gaps, and assess deployment readiness across sensing modalities. A systematic literature search was conducted across IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar following PRISMA guidelines, covering studies published between January 2023 and December 2025. From an initial pool of 120 articles, 45 human-subject experimental studies met the inclusion criteria. Included studies were categorized into four sensing modalities: pressure-based, wearable sensor-based, vision- and imaging-based, and contactless radio-frequency (RF) and radar-based systems. Standardized data extraction covered dataset characteristics, preprocessing methods, learning models, sensing hardware, posture classes, and performance metrics. Most studies focused on four primary posture classes - supine, prone, left lateral, and right lateral - and reported high accuracy, mostly under controlled laboratory conditions. However, subject-independent validation was not consistently applied, and few studies examined finer-grained posture taxonomies. Recurring limitations, including private datasets and insufficient cross-subject validation, highlight the need for open benchmark datasets, standardized evaluation protocols, and deployment-oriented assessment to advance reliable and generalizable sleep posture recognition systems.

papers.title: Ketamine's mechanisms of action in major depressive disorder and treatment-resistant depression: Is brain topological change a candidate convergent systems-level pathway?
papers.abstract: Ketamine is a rapid-acting antidepressant with demonstrated efficacy in major depressive disorder and treatment-resistant depression, yet the mechanisms by which its molecular actions translate into sustained clinical improvement remain incompletely understood. Prevailing models have emphasized N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor antagonism and downstream glutamatergic signaling; however, convergent evidence indicates that ketamine engages a broader hierarchy of biological processes spanning synaptic plasticity, circuit dynamics, and large-scale brain network organization. This narrative review integrates molecular, cellular, circuit-level, neuroimaging, and electrophysiological findings to evaluate whether normalization of pathological brain topology represents a convergent systems-level pathway mediating ketamine's antidepressant effects. Across modalities, depressive disorders are characterized by disrupted network integration and segregation, stability of maladaptive configurations, and impaired flexibility of large-scale neural systems. Evidence from functional magnetic resonance imaging and electroencephalography indicates that ketamine rapidly modulates these abnormalities, increasing global connectivity, reducing rigid network organization, and enhancing neural signal diversity and network dynamics. These effects emerge within hours, are associated with clinical improvement, and show temporal and mechanistic distinctions from those observed with monoaminergic antidepressants, neuromodulation, psychotherapy, and serotonergic psychedelics. Integrating these findings, this review proposes that ketamine's molecular and circuit-level actions are necessary but not sufficient, with antidepressant efficacy shaped by how these processes are instantiated within large-scale network topology. Conceptualizing brain topology as an integrative systems-level framework may help reconcile diverse mechanistic observations, clarify sources of treatment resistance, and inform testable hypotheses for topology-based biomarkers and novel rapid-acting antidepressant strategies.

papers.title: Basic-level category processing advantage in fear generalization and its modulation by threat-conditioned stimulus diversity: Behavioral and event-related potential evidence.
papers.abstract: Category-based fear generalization refers to the extension of acquired fear responses to novel stimuli sharing categorical cues with a threat stimulus. Categories are organized into superordinate, basic-level, and subordinate levels, which differ in cognitive processing advantages; however, whether this categorical advantage influences fear generalization remains unclear. Experiment 1 used a discriminative fear conditioning paradigm, employing subordinate exemplars of birds and measuring tools as the threat-conditioned stimulus (CS+) and the safety-conditioned stimulus (CS-), respectively. During the generalization test, we included generalization stimuli sharing either the same basic-level category (GSBasic) or the same superordinate category (but different basic-level category) as the CS+. Fear generalization was assessed via shock expectancy ratings and skin conductance responses. Experiment 2 manipulated CS+ diversity (high vs. low) in the same task while recording electroencephalography to examine its moderating role. Behaviorally, acquired fear generalized more robustly to GSBasic than to GS sharing the same superordinate category (GSSuperordinate). Participants in the high-diversity group showed higher shock expectancy ratings for both the CS+ and GSBasic than those in the low-diversity group. Event-related potential results revealed that GSBasic elicited P2 and N400 amplitudes comparable to those of the CS+, and exhibited more positive P2 and less negative N400 amplitudes than GSSuperordinate and CS-. Moreover, only the CS+ and GSBasic elicited more positive LPP amplitudes than CS-. These findings suggest that early attentional allocation, late semantic processing, and motivational attention collectively constitute the electrophysiological basis of the basic-level category processing advantage in fear generalization, offering implications for the intervention of anxiety disorders.

papers.title: Rapid screening of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in port sediments using multiblock spectroscopy and hierarchical classification.
papers.abstract: Marine petroleum hydrocarbon contamination remains a persistent concern in port environments, where polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) can accumulate in sediments and pose long-term ecological risks. However, routine PAH assessment relies on labor-intensive laboratory analyses, which can restrict monitoring frequency and spatial coverage. This study developed a rapid screening framework for PAH contamination in port sediments using simplified solvent extraction, portable spectrophotometry, and multiblock hierarchical classification based on ultraviolet fluorescence, ultraviolet transmission, and visible transmission spectra. A total of 277 sediment samples were collected from 10 major ports in South Korea. Among these, 124 samples from four ports were analyzed for PAHs by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, yielding total PAH concentrations ranging from 13.7 to 8170 ng·g-1 dry weight, and were used for model development and validation. The optimized hierarchical model was evaluated using Venetian-blinds internal cross-validation and an external validation set excluded from model development, achieving classification accuracies of 0.87-0.90 across the four contamination categories. These results suggest that the proposed framework can support rapid, screening-level identification of PAH contamination gradients and potential hotspots in port sediments, thereby complementing conventional chemical analysis for sediment monitoring and management.

papers.title: Rosmarinic acid- and epigallocatechin gallate-enriched extracts improve insomnia and sleep-wake balance in caffeine-and p-chlorophenylalanine-induced insomnia models.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of a rosmarinic acid- and epigallocatechin gallate-enriched extract mixture (RE-GTE) on insomnia and sleep-wake disturbances induced by excessive caffeine intake or serotonin depletion using p-chlorophenylalanine (PCPA) in mice. RE-GTE was administered in both caffeine- and PCPA-induced insomnia models, and sleep-related behaviors were assessed using pentobarbital-induced sleep tests and behavioral analyses of anxiety-related and locomotor parameters. In addition, sleep-related neurotransmitters and receptor expression were examined using molecular and biochemical approaches. In the caffeine-induced insomnia model, RE-GTE supplementation significantly attenuated caffeine-induced dopaminergic hyperactivity, increased gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) levels, and improved anxiety-related and selected locomotor behavioral parameters. RE-GTE also upregulated GABAA receptor expression while reducing adenosine A1 and A2A receptor expression, accompanied by increased sleep duration. In the PCPA-induced insomnia model, RE-GTE increased hypothalamic serotonin and melatonin levels, reduced stress-related hormones including adrenocorticotropic hormone and corticosterone, increased serotonin receptor expression, and reduced overexpression of the orexin 2 receptor, indicating selective modulation of serotonergic and stress-related markers. Across both models, high-dose RE-GTE (40 mg/kg) increased sleep duration toward normal levels. Collectively, these findings indicate that RE-GTE ameliorates insomnia-related behavioral and neurochemical disturbances and that this improvement is accompanied by selective changes in adenosinergic, GABAergic, and serotonergic markers. These pathway-level associations support further investigation of RE-GTE as a promising natural candidate for the management of sleep disturbances.

papers.title: Wellness4Teachers Supportive Text Messaging Program Association with Observed Improvement in Psychological Symptoms Among Teachers in Canada: A Single-arm Prospective Longitudinal and Naturalistic Controlled Study.
papers.abstract: Wellness4Teachers is a daily supportive text messaging program implemented to mitigate psychological distress and support the wellbeing of teachers in Canada. To assess whether Wellness4Teachers can reduce the severity and prevalence of psychological issues and improve resilience among teachers in Alberta, Newfoundland and Labrador, and Nova Scotia. This study used a single-arm prospective longitudinal design with a secondary exploratory naturalistic contemporaneous comparison. Teachers self-subscribed to Wellness4Teachers text messaging program for six months, and completed web-based surveys. The program was launched at the beginning of the 2022-2023 academic year. Longitudinal outcomes were assessed at baseline, six weeks, three months, and six months. The naturalistic comparison included an intervention group (IG) who received messages for six months and completed six-month assessments between March 1 and June 30, 2023, and a comparison group (CG) who enrolled and completed baseline assessments during the same period before receiving messages. Standardized scales were used for assessing psychological symptoms. Likely Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD), likely Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), resilience, burnout, and stress were assessed using the GAD-7 scale, the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ)-9, the Brief Resilience Scale, the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Educator Survey (MBI-ES) and the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) respectively. Data analysis was conducted using SPSS (version 28.0). Paired-samples t-tests assessed longitudinal changes, while independent-samples t-tests compared groups. McNemar and chi-square tests examined categorical variables. Missing follow-up data were addressed using last observation carried forward, with sensitivity analyses comparing baseline scores with those at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months. Independent-samples t-tests and chi-square tests compared baseline psychological scores and categorical characteristics between follow-up completers and non-completers. In the longitudinal analysis, PSS-10, MBI-EE subscale, PHQ-9, PHQ-9 Item 3 (sleep disturbance), PHQ-9 Item 9 (suicidal ideation/self-harm), and GAD-7 scores decreased significantly at six months by 5.50% (MD=1.29, 95% CI:0.86-1.72), 4.48% (MD=1.67, 95% CI:0.43-2.92), 18.58% (MD=2.10, 95% CI:1.39-2.80), 17.54% (MD=0.30, 95% CI:0.15-0.44), 37.50% (MD=0.09, 95% CI:0.02-0.17), and 13.52% (MD=1.30, 95% CI:0.62-1.99), respectively. Likely MDD decreased from 55.2% (n=116) to 41.0% (n=86), a 14.2% reduction. In the exploratory contemporaneous comparison, the IG (n=166) had lower PSS-10 (6.04%; MD= -1.41, 95% CI: -2.17 to -0.65), PHQ-9 (21.16%; MD= -2.33, 95% CI: -3.59 to -1.06), and GAD-7 (22.48%; MD= -2.19, 95% CI: -3.39 to -0.98) scores than the CG (n=152). Likely MDD and GAD prevalence were 20.6% and 20.3% lower, respectively. Adjusted analyses showed intervention-group status was associated with lower odds of high stress (OR=0.42, 95% CI:0.19-0.95), likely MDD (OR=0.47, 95% CI:0.28-0.81), and likely GAD (OR=0.37, 95% CI:0.21-0.64). Wellness4Teachers was associated with improvements in several psychological outcomes over six months and may offer a promising approach to support teachers' psychological wellbeing. RR2-10.2196/37934.

papers.title: The qualitative exploration of work productivity among chronic rhinitis patients.
papers.abstract: Chronic rhinitis is a global public health concern affecting sleep, cognitive function, mood, quality of life, and work performance. It contributes to socioeconomic costs through decreased productivity, including absenteeism and presenteeism. This study explores the impact of chronic rhinitis on work productivity and employee performance to inform better management strategies. A literature review and semi-structured interviews were conducted with 19 chronic rhinitis patients from Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz and Hospital Ampang. Data saturation was reached, and thematic analysis was performed using Atlas.ti. Eight themes were identified: absence during working hours, work limitations, disruption of social interactions, reduced work efficiency, emotional disturbances, weaknesses in compliance with work procedures, sleepiness at work, and negative perceptions from colleagues. Chronic rhinitis significantly affects work productivity, leading to absenteeism, reduced efficiency, and workplace stigma. These findings highlight the need for targeted management strategies to improve work performance and reduce the negative impact of chronic rhinitis on affected individuals.

papers.title: Vitamin D Supplementation and Improvement in Insomnia Symptoms Among Malaysian Women With Vitamin D Deficiency: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder associated with adverse physical, psychological, and functional outcomes. Emerging evidence suggests that vitamin D deficiency may contribute to sleep disturbances. Women are more likely to have lower serum vitamin D (25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D]) levels than men, and they also report a higher prevalence of insomnia. Although several studies have proposed that vitamin D supplementation may improve insomnia symptoms, findings remain inconsistent, and evidence from Southeast Asian populations is limited. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of weekly vitamin D₃ supplementation in improving insomnia symptoms, sleep quality, sleep efficiency, and functional outcomes among Malaysian women with vitamin D deficiency. This study is a double-blind, parallel-group, randomized placebo-controlled trial conducted among women aged 19-50 years with serum 25(OH)D levels <20 ng/mL and insomnia symptoms. Participants are randomized to receive either vitamin D₃ capsules (50,000 IU/wk) or placebo (1 capsule/wk) for 9 weeks. The study is conducted in a community setting. Primary outcomes include insomnia severity assessed using the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), sleep quality measured by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and sleep efficiency objectively assessed using actigraphy. Secondary outcomes include daytime sleepiness measured using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and functional outcomes assessed using the Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire (FOSQ-10). Assessments are conducted at baseline, midintervention, and postintervention. Participant recruitment commenced in December 2023 and is expected to conclude in December 2026. As of July 2026, 42 participants had been screened, 33 eligible participants had been enrolled, 22 had completed the study procedures, 4 were in the intervention phase, and 1 had withdrawn due to loss of contact. If the efficacy of vitamin D3 supplementation in alleviating insomnia symptoms is demonstrated, it might be proposed as a supplementary approach to cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for insomnia. Screening for vitamin D deficiency may also be considered in individuals presenting with insomnia symptoms prior to initiating pharmacological treatment.

papers.title: Nonlinear Feature Modeling Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Electroencephalography for Depression Classification: Deep Learning Study.
papers.abstract: Depression is a common mental disorder that seriously affects mental health and quality of life. Traditional depression diagnosis mainly relies on clinical interviews and subjective assessments, which may lead to variability in diagnostic outcomes. Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based computer-aided diagnosis has emerged as a promising, objective approach for depression recognition. However, effectively modeling the complex nonlinear characteristics of EEG signals remains a major challenge for existing deep learning methods. This study aimed to investigate the applicability of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) for EEG-based depression recognition and to evaluate the effectiveness of KAN-based nonlinear modeling frameworks on frequency-domain EEG features. KAN was introduced into EEG-based depression recognition to enhance nonlinear feature representation of brain electrical signals. Two representative KAN-based convolutional architectures, ConvKAN and its efficiency-optimized variant ConvKAN Efficient, were systematically investigated for EEG classification tasks. These architectures incorporated KANLinear layers together with dynamic grid updating, enhanced weight initialization, and regularization strategies to improve nonlinear modeling capability while maintaining computational efficiency. Extensive experiments were conducted on the EDRA dataset, and the proposed framework was compared with conventional convolutional neural network-based methods and traditional machine learning approaches. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. Experimental results demonstrated that the KAN-based frameworks achieved superior EEG classification performance compared with conventional convolutional neural network-based methods and traditional machine learning approaches. Among the evaluated models, ConvKAN Efficient achieved the best overall performance, with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score all exceeding 94% on the EDRA dataset. The results indicate that KAN-based architectures can effectively capture the complex nonlinear characteristics of EEG signals while preserving high computational efficiency. This study systematically demonstrates the applicability of KAN-based nonlinear modeling frameworks to EEG-based depression recognition. The proposed framework provides a scalable and effective approach for EEG signal analysis and offers valuable technical support for both theoretical research and clinical applications in computer-aided depression recognition.

papers.title: Negative impact of a 1-month period of night shifts on mental and physical health among Swiss internal medicine residents.
papers.abstract: To assess the impact of short periods of night shifts on: sleep quality and sleep medication intake, burnout scores, care-related regrets experience and coping mechanisms of internal medicine residents. Before-after analysis of data from the Nightshift project, a repeated measures evaluation of the clinical activity and burden of night shifts, conducted between October 2019 and March 2020 in the Division of General Internal Medicine of Geneva University Hospitals (Clinicaltrials.gov: NCT04123015). Forty-one residents of 55 (74.5%) screened for eligibility were included before their first night shift. They completed an anonymous e-survey before and after a 1-month period of night shifts, assessing sleep quality, sleep medication intake, burnout scores using the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI), the number and intensity of care-related regrets using the Regret Intensity Scale (RIS-10) and resident's coping abilities with the Care-related Regret Coping Scale for Health-care Professionals (RCS-HCP). After the 1-month period of night shifts, sleep medication intake had increased from 7.3% to 24.4%, p = 0.02. At baseline, 31 (75.6%) of the 41 participating residents (65.9% women) scored low in all three dimensions of burnout. For each burnout dimension, at least 30% of residents had an increase in score ≥5 points. Moderate or high levels of burnout remained stable for professional burnout (24.4%), but increased for personal (17.1% to 26.9%) and patient-related burnout (4.8% to 14.6%) though none of these changes were statistically significant. All of the 25% of residents who experienced regrets on actions taken during their shift were women. They reported overall limited coping abilities, e.g. 80% displayed frequent use of negative maladaptive strategies to deal with regret. Even short periods of night shifts can have a significant impact on residents' mental and physical health. A high proportion of residents had increased burnout scores, a factor known to be correlated with job dissatisfaction and absence due to sickness. Sleep medication intake increased 3-fold, suggesting sleep issues. Respondents reported frequent care-related regrets and poor coping abilities, with use of maladaptive strategies, known to be associated with poor sleep and job resignation. As stricter regulations on daily working hours are proposed, the frequency of on-call duties will inevitably increase. Understanding the implications of short periods of night shifts is not only essential for shaping residency programme policies and for shift scheduling, but also for informing training programmes on non-pharmacological sleep management, burnout prevention and the development of positive regret-coping strategies.

papers.title: Parental Anxiety, Depression, and Sleep Quality in Relation to Infant Sleep: A Two-Cohort Longitudinal Study.
papers.abstract: Parental mental health is linked to infant sleep, but research has focused mainly on mothers and on single distress dimensions. This study examined whether parental anxiety, depression, and sleep quality are associated with infant sleep across the first year, and whether mothers and fathers contribute differently. Two independent cohorts of Taiwanese families (42 and 80 infants; 107 and 270 observations) were followed across the first year, assessed at 1-6 months (Cohort 1) and 1-12 months (Cohort 2). At each assessment, both parents completed the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and infant sleep was assessed by a sleep diary and the Brief Infant Sleep Questionnaire. Linear mixed-effects models with standardized predictors treated one cohort as discovery and the second as replication. Poorer maternal sleep quality was associated with more parent-perceived night awakenings in both cohorts (b = 0.28 and 0.48), the only association that replicated. In the larger cohort, poorer maternal sleep quality was also associated with shorter nighttime sleep. Parental anxiety, depression, and paternal sleep quality showed no consistent associations. Maternal sleep quality was the most robust parental correlate of infant sleep, most evident for perceived night awakenings. Extending a literature that has centered on maternal mood, these findings point to maternal sleep quality as a distinct correlate; in perinatal care, brief screening of maternal sleep quality may help flag families who could benefit from sleep-focused guidance or referral.

papers.title: Passive Hyperthermia Increases Neural Recruitment, Thereby Reducing Processing Efficiency During Executive Task Performance.
papers.abstract: Heat-induced hyperthermia impairs cognitive performance and contributes to central fatigue during exercise and environmental heat exposure. Electroencephalographic event-related potential (EEG-ERP) studies consistently show reduced P300 amplitudes under heat stress, whereas functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies often report expanded blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) activation. This study examined how passive hyperthermia influences task-dependent neural activation and cognitive processing using both fMRI and EEG-ERP within comparable paradigms. Eighteen healthy adults (ten males and eight females) performed Go/No-go and Flanker tasks under normothermic and hyperthermic conditions during fMRI. Passive heating increased external ear canal temperature (Tear) by approximately 1.1°C above baseline. Sixteen participants completed an additional EEG-ERP session with the Flanker task. Behavioral responses, regional BOLD activation, and P300 amplitude and latency were assessed. Cervical arterial blood flow was measured by using a color-coded ultrasound system. The mean heating duration was 53.9 ± 9.2 min across all subjects. Hyperthermia increased heart rate and Tear while reducing internal carotid and vertebral artery blood flow. Reaction times decreased in both tasks, with no change in error rates. fMRI showed expanded activation in bilateral frontal, parietal, temporal, and subcortical regions. Task subtraction analyses (Flanker minus Go/No-go) revealed greater frontal and parietal activation during the complex task. In contrast, P300 amplitude was reduced during hyperthermia. Passive hyperthermia expands the spatial extent task-related BOLD activation while reducing P300 amplitude, suggesting reduced processing efficiency. However, the BOLD findings should be interpreted with caution because cerebral perfusion was also reduced. These findings suggest increased neural strain under heat stress, contributing to central fatigue and potentially impairing decision-making in sport and occupational setting.
papers.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

papers.title: REM Atonia Index Cutoffs for REM Sleep Without Atonia: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis of Adult Diagnostic Performance.
papers.abstract: To synthesize evidence on REM Atonia Index (RAI) thresholds and reference values, quantify adult diagnostic performance for REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), and distinguish diagnostic cutoffs from physiological reference limits and pediatric values. Methods: We conducted a focused systematic review of studies using automated RAI, rescreening studies from a previous review and updating PubMed/MEDLINE through July 27, 2026. Adult diagnostic accuracy was synthesized with a bivariate binomial-normal random-effects model. Continuous RAI differences were pooled as raw mean differences. Normative adult and pediatric evidence was synthesized separately because these represented different estimands. The review was retrospectively registered in OSF Registries on August 20, 2026 (https://osf.io/v3kqa). Thirty unique studies were included. Eight adult studies contributed to the diagnostic-accuracy meta-analysis; thresholds ranged from 0.80 to 0.90. Pooled sensitivity was 0.850 (95% CI, 0.766-0.908) and specificity 0.895 (95% CI, 0.814-0.944). Eight studies contributed continuous data; RAI was lower in RBD by a pooled mean difference of -0.263 (95% CI, -0.335 to -0.190). Only two methodologically non-equivalent adult studies provided physiological reference limits, 0.85 and 0.91, precluding pooling. Pediatric evidence supported age-conditioned interpretation. Adult chin-EMG RAI shows good overall discrimination of established RBD, but current evidence does not support a universal numerical boundary for REM sleep without atonia. Evidence defining physiological reference limits is substantially less developed than diagnostic evidence, and normal RAI varies with age. RAI should therefore be reported continuously, with thresholds interpreted according to their intended diagnostic or physiological purpose.

papers.title: Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome: Unloading the Respiratory System with Expiratory Pressure.
papers.abstract: Obesity hypoventilation syndrome (OHS) is traditionally interpreted through the lens of coexistent obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), yet the mechanisms by which continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) improves daytime hypercapnia without providing ventilatory support remain incompletely explained. This Perspective proposes that abdominal obesity-induced depletion of expiratory reserve volume (ERV) and functional residual capacity (FRC), with consequent reduction in end-expiratory lung volume (EELV), may represent upstream mechanical abnormalities linking OSA, increased work of breathing, sleep hypoventilation, and daytime hypercapnia. Reduced EELV worsens pharyngeal collapsibility by decreasing caudal traction, while simultaneously shifting tidal volume toward a mechanically inefficient portion of the respiratory system curve, characterized by impaired compliance, and increased elastic, resistive respiratory work and possibly threshold loading. Within this framework, OHS emerges when respiratory burden (the mechanical load on the pulmonary apparatus due to excess weight) exceeds ventilatory reserve (an ensemble of respiratory drive and its modifiers such as sleep-state control, leptin signaling, and genetic factors). CPAP and expiratory PAP may provide, in addition to upper-airway splinting, a mechanical unloading by raising EELV, improving respiratory mechanics, and reducing the pressure cost of ventilation. In this context, weight loss represents the ultimate structural unloading therapy, whereas pressure support may be required when unloading alone is insufficient to restore adequate ventilation. Future studies should measure ERV, FRC/EELV, respiratory effort, and mechanics to better phenotype OHS, and understand whether optimizing expiratory pressure before adding ventilatory support actually improves ventilation.

papers.title: Bridging the Gap Between Design and Access: Toward Visual Scene Displays for Brain-Computer Interface Use in Augmentative and Alternative Communication by Children.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) may support communication and computer interaction through neural signals such as the P300 event-related potential (ERP). As a step toward integrating photographic visual scene displays (VSDs) in BCI, this study examined the feasibility of incorporating contextual, naturalistic scenes in which communication items were embedded asymmetrically. To evaluate the effects of contextual scene use, 24 neurotypical children aged 8-13 years completed three experimental conditions: (1) a contextual scene with asymmetrical item placement, (2) an asymmetrical arrangement of the same items without contextual information, and (3) a standard grid. Electroencephalogram data were analyzed for the N170, P300, and N400 ERP components, and offline (predicted) BCI augmentative and alternative communication accuracy was calculated. The results showed that asymmetry increased frontal and centro-parietal P300 amplitudes, and the scene enhanced occipital N170. Offline BCI performance was similar across the scene and grid conditions, and participants rated the scene as more visually appealing. These findings indicate that asymmetry and contextual embedding within scenes may enhance neural engagement and user experience, providing a preliminary foundation for considering photographic VSDs into pediatric BCI research.
papers.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR

papers.title: Template-Anchored Signal Decomposition and Label Refinement for Impairment Categorization on Noisy Visual Electrophysiological Data.
papers.abstract: Visual electrophysiology offers an objective alternative to subjective vision assessments, providing enhanced reliability but remaining underutilized for visual impairment categorization due to imperfect datasets, noisy signals, and label inconsistencies. To address these challenges, we first construct a new dataset comprising ERG and VEP recordings from 1,970 participants with various ocular conditions and a mean age of 21.59 $\pm$ 4.47 years. A three-class categorization task is defined to reflect clinical disability grading. We then propose a template-anchored decomposition method for noise-aware signal feature extraction, using mode-specific ridge regression to isolate pathological components by removing both healthy patterns and noise artifacts. To collectively enhance feature representation from multi-channel signals, we design a joint attention encoder that combines channel attention with bilateral spatial attention across left- and right-eye channels to emphasize informative and coherent signal patterns. Furthermore, we introduce a template-anchored refinement mechanism that addresses label noise by updating soft labels during training based on the distances between each feature vector and the class templates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves consistent improvements over existing electrophysiology-based and general biosignal classification methods, supporting its feasibility for visual impairment categorization in a cohort composed primarily of young adults.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

papers.title: Patient Characteristics and Anesthetic Factors Affecting Hospital Length of Stay in Orthognathic Surgery.
papers.abstract: As orthognathic surgery increasingly shifts toward ambulatory pathways, identifying patients at risk for extended length of stay (eLOS) remains clinically important. This study evaluated preoperative patient characteristics and anesthetic factors associated with eLOS after orthognathic surgery. A retrospective cohort study was performed of patients who underwent Le Fort I osteotomy at a single tertiary academic center between 2019 and 2025. Demographic, airway-related, anesthetic, and operative variables were extracted from the electronic medical record. The primary outcome was eLOS, defined as hospitalization of 2 or more days. Patients were compared by length-of-stay cohort, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors. The study included 170 patients, of whom 47 experienced eLOS. On unadjusted analysis, patients with eLOS had higher rates of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), difficult airway history, elevated Mallampati class, ASA class III status, and longer anesthesia and operative durations.
